interest: Peru's confused handling of Nisei Fernando Abey's nationality.
keywords: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser
overview: This file (State Department decimal file 894.22/3-3048 through 894.22/5-1348) documents diplomatic correspondence between the Embassy of Peru in Washington and the U.S. Department of State regarding Fernando Ychiro Abey, a Peruvian-born man of Japanese parentage residing in Yokohama. At the request of the Peruvian Embassy, the Department directed the Yokohama Branch of the Office of the U.S. Political Adviser (USPOLAD) to investigate whether Abey had served in the Japanese armed forces during World War II. The investigation revealed that Abey had arrived in Japan in 1941, was kept under strict Japanese police surveillance during the war, and had never served in the Japanese military, though he was recently noted by local water police for trafficking in black-market fish under the protection of his claimed foreign status. Internal State Department reviews connected this inquiry with an earlier 1947 transit visa application by Abey, uncovering that the Peruvian Foreign Office had already ruled in March 1948 that Abey had lost his Peruvian nationality due to residence in Japan during his minority. The State Department closed the exchange in June 1948 by reporting the negative finding on military service while diplomatically reminding the Peruvian Embassy of their own government's prior determination of his loss of citizenship.
